eq_cardio_treadmill.name: Treadmill

steps.title: Safety stop
steps.text: Locate Stop and attach the safety clip to clothing if provided; test it as instructed by the manufacturer.

steps.title: Starting position
steps.text: Mount using the fixed platforms and handrails according to the machine's placard; start the belt at its lowest walking speed.

steps.title: Speed and incline
steps.text: Increase one setting gradually while keeping a natural gait. Slow down instead of hanging from the rails.

steps.title: Dismount
steps.text: Reduce speed, stop the belt fully, and use the rails to step off. Never jump onto or off a moving belt.

eq_cardio_treadmill.caution: Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.

eq_cardio_stairs.name: Stair machine

steps.title: Mount safely
steps.text: Find the stop control and use fixed steps and handrails to mount with the machine stopped, following its placard.

steps.title: Foot placement
steps.text: Face forward and place enough of each foot securely on the tread; keep shoes clear of moving edges.

steps.title: Step speed
steps.text: Begin at the lowest pace and increase gradually. Stay upright with light rail contact rather than supporting bodyweight on the arms.

steps.title: Stop and descend
steps.text: Slow and stop the steps fully before dismounting with the handrails. Record steps/min and floors from the console when available.

eq_cardio_stairs.caution: Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.

eq_cardio_bike.name: Exercise bike

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: With the pedal farthest away, keep a small knee bend without rocking the hips. Adjust and lock the seat while stopped.

steps.title: Reach and feet
steps.text: Set the seat and handlebar reach for relaxed shoulders. Secure shoes using the intended pedal straps; keep laces clear.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Start at low resistance and learn the model's braking controls. Fixed-gear pedals keep moving with the flywheel; use its brake before dismounting.

steps.title: Console
steps.text: Select time and distance display units. Record resistance as the machine's setting; levels are not comparable across models.

eq_cardio_bike.caution: Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.

eq_cardio_rower.name: Rowing machine

steps.title: Foot supports
steps.text: Adjust the heel cups so the straps cross the widest part of the feet. Snug the straps without cutting circulation.

steps.title: Seat and travel
steps.text: Check the seat slides smoothly and the rail is clear. Sit balanced with relaxed shoulders and a secure, light handle grip.

steps.title: Resistance or damper
steps.text: Start with an easy setting and learn the stroke. An air damper changes airflow and stroke feel; it is not a universal resistance or intensity scale.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Choose time and distance, normally meters, and begin with easy strokes. Park the handle safely and release the straps before standing.

eq_cardio_rower.caution: Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.

safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Build total duration gradually before adding harder intervals.
Use an easy warm-up and cool-down, and reduce impact if joints become painful.
mistakes: Overstriding: shorten the stride and keep foot contacts controlled.
Increasing pace and incline abruptly: change one setting gradually.
Leaning on treadmill rails: reduce speed or incline until you can move with light balance support only.

safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Recheck seat adjustment if knee or hip discomfort appears.
Learn the machine's braking behavior before attempting hard intervals.
mistakes: Rocking the hips: check seat height and reduce resistance.
Grinding against excessive resistance: lower the setting and restore smooth pedal motion.
Dismounting while fixed-gear pedals turn: brake and wait for a complete stop.

safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Use slower practice strokes before increasing power or stroke rate.
Keep the grip light and stop if the back or wrists become painful.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms before driving the legs: restore the legs-body-arms sequence.
Rounding or throwing the lower back: shorten the reach and control the hip hinge.
Treating maximum damper as the best workout: learn technique at an easy setting; record the machine setting separately from effort.

safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Build repetitions gradually and allow enough recovery between sets.
Use step jacks for less impact if jumping causes discomfort.
mistakes: Landing with stiff knees: soften the landing and reduce jump height.
Knees collapsing inward: slow down and keep knees aligned with the feet.
Forcing the arms overhead through pain: use a comfortable reach or a step-jack variation.

safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Start with short bouts and increase time as balance and conditioning allow.
Use a secure handrail and keep clear of moving step edges.
mistakes: Skipping treads at an uncontrolled pace: return to single, secure steps.
Supporting bodyweight on the rails: lower speed and restore upright posture.
Turning around on moving steps: remain forward-facing and stop before dismounting.
